stem:
Ira compares broad, flat green leaves with narrow green leaves on plants making food.

Why does the broad, flat shape help the leaves make food?

options.text: A broad, flat shape gives a large surface to receive sunlight, so the leaves can make more food.
A broad, flat shape lets the leaves make food in complete darkness.
A broad, flat shape spreads sunlight more thinly, so those leaves make less food than the narrow leaves under the same light.
The green colour alone makes the food, so the broad, flat shape does not matter.

teacher.key_rationale: Broad, flat leaves present a large surface to sunlight, so more food can be made. Darkness omits the light condition; thinner spreading reverses the efficiency claim; colour alone is a surface feature that ignores shape.
